title.zh: 第十四 五行二 災火 草妖 羽蟲孽 羊禍
title.raw: 第十四 五行二 災火 草妖 羽蟲孽 羊禍 Volume 104: Five Elements Part Two

sentences.zh: 志第十四 五行二

translations.literal: Treatise, the fourteenth: Five Elements, part two.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise Fourteen: The Five Elements, Part Two.

sentences.zh: 灾火 草妖 羽虫孽 羊祸

translations.literal: Calamitous fire; grass prodigies; winged-creature prodigies; sheep disasters.
translations.idiomatic: Fire as disaster; freak growths among plants; plagues among fowl and winged pests; calamities involving sheep.

sentences.zh: 《五行傳》曰：「弃法律，逐功臣，殺太子，以妾为妻，则火不炎上。

translations.literal: The Treatise on the Five Elements says: "If one casts aside laws and statutes, drives away meritorious ministers, kills the heir apparent, and takes a concubine as wife, then fire will not blaze upward."
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on the Five Elements warns that when laws are trampled, good servants banished, the crown prince murdered, and a concubine raised to wife, the virtue of fire fails—it no longer "blazes upward" as it should.

sentences.zh: 」谓火失其性而为灾也。

translations.literal: " This means that fire loses its nature and becomes a disaster.
translations.idiomatic: That is, fire’s nature is corrupted and calamity follows.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「视之不明，是谓不悊。

translations.literal: It also says: "When insight is not clear, this is called lack of discernment (bu zhe)."
translations.idiomatic: It adds: "When the ruler’s vision clouds over, that is called a failure of wise judgment."

sentences.zh: 厥咎舒，厥罚常燠，厥极疾，时则有草妖，时则有蠃虫之孽，时则有羊祸，时则有赤眚、赤祥，惟水沴火。

translations.literal: Its fault is slackness; its punishment is constant heat; its extreme is sickness; then there are grass prodigies, then naked-soft insect prodigies, then sheep disasters, then red calamities and red auspices—only water injures fire.
translations.idiomatic: The blame falls on lax rule; the scourge is endless summer heat; the worst end is pestilence; such times bring freaks among plants, plagues among soft-bodied vermin, omens involving sheep, and crimson spectral fires—and in the cycle of qi, water is said to harm fire.

sentences.zh: 」蠃虫，刘歆傳以为羽虫。

translations.literal: " Naked-soft insects—in Liu Xin’s transmission they are taken to be winged creatures.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary following Liu Xin classes those "soft" pests with omens among winged things.

sentences.zh: 建武中，渔阳太守彭宠被征。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era, Yuyang prefect Peng Chong was summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangwu’s Jianwu years the summons reached Peng Chong, governor of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 书至，明日潞县火，灾起城中，飞出城外，燔千余家，殺人。

translations.literal: When the letter arrived, the next day Lu county caught fire; the disaster began inside the city, flew out beyond the wall, burned more than a thousand households, and killed people.
translations.idiomatic: The day after the edict arrived, Lu county erupted in a fire that started downtown, leaped the walls, consumed over a thousand homes, and killed many.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「上不俭，下不節，盛火数起，燔宫室。

translations.literal: Jing Fang’s Commentary on the Changes says: "If above is not frugal and below is not restrained, flourishing fires arise repeatedly and burn palace halls."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang warns that when neither court nor country practices restraint, palace fires break out again and again.

sentences.zh: 」儒说火以明为德而主礼。

translations.literal: " Ru learning holds that fire takes brightness as its virtue and presides over ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian exegetes say fire’s virtue is clarity and its domain is ritual.

sentences.zh: 时宠与幽州牧朱浮有隙，疑浮见浸谮，故意狐疑，其妻劝无应征，遂反叛攻浮，卒诛灭。

translations.literal: At the time Chong had a rift with Youzhou shepherd Zhu Fu; he suspected Fu was slandering him by degrees, so he deliberately hesitated; his wife urged him not to answer the summons, whereupon he rebelled and attacked Fu, and in the end was executed and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Chong had quarreled with the regional inspector Zhu Fu, brooded on slander, and—on his wife’s advice—defied the recall; he rose against Zhu Fu and was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 和帝永元八年十二月丁巳，南宫宣室殿火。

translations.literal: In Emperor He’s eighth year of Yongyuan, twelfth month, day dingsi, the Xuanshi Hall of the Southern Palace burned.
translations.idiomatic: On a dingsi day in the twelfth month of Yongyuan 8 the Xuanshi Hall in the Southern Palace caught fire.

sentences.zh: 是时和帝幸北宫，窦太后在南宫。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor He favored the Northern Palace; Empress Dowager Dou was in the Southern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was spending his nights in the Northern Palace while Empress Dowager Dou remained in the south.

sentences.zh: 明年，窦太后崩。

translations.literal: The next year Empress Dowager Dou died.
translations.idiomatic: She died the following year.

sentences.zh: 十三年八月己亥，北宫盛馔门阁火。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, eighth month, day jihai, the Shengzhuan Gate tower of the Northern Palace burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Yongyuan 13 fire destroyed the Shengzhuan gate-tower of the Northern Palace.

sentences.zh: 是时和帝幸邓贵人，阴后宠衰怨恨，上有欲废之意。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor He favored Honored Lady Deng; Empress Yin’s favor waned and she nursed resentment; above there was intent to depose her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor He had turned to Lady Deng while Empress Yin, fallen from favor, smoldered with hate; the emperor meant to cast her off.

sentences.zh: 明年，会得阴后挟伪道事，遂废，迁于桐宫，以忧死，立邓贵人为皇后。

translations.literal: The next year, meeting the affair of Empress Yin practicing false Daoism, she was thereupon deposed, removed to the Tong palace, died of grief, and Honored Lady Deng was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Yin empress was caught in a sorcery scandal, stripped of rank, confined to the Cold Palace, and left to die of shame; Lady Deng became empress in her place.

sentences.zh: 十五年六月辛酉，汉中城固南城门灾。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, sixth month, day xinyou, the south gate of Chenggu in Hanzhong suffered fire disaster.
translations.idiomatic: On a xinyou day in the sixth month of Yongyuan 15 the south gate of Chenggu in Hanzhong burned.

sentences.zh: 此孝和皇帝将绝世之象也。

translations.literal: This was an image of Emperor Xiaohe’s line about to end.
translations.idiomatic: It foretold the extinction of Emperor He’s line.

sentences.zh: 其后二年，宫车晏驾，殇帝及平原王皆早夭折，和帝世绝。

translations.literal: After two more years the palace carriage tarried; Emperor Shang and the Prince of Pingyuan both died young, and He’s posterity was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years the emperor was dead, the boy emperor and the prince of Pingyuan followed him to the grave, and He left no heir.

sentences.zh: 安帝永初二年四月甲寅，汉阳阿阳城中失火，烧殺三千五百七十人。

translations.literal: In Emperor An’s second year of Yongchu, fourth month, day jiayin, fire broke out in Ayang city in Hanyang, burning to death three thousand five hundred seventy people.
translations.idiomatic: On an jiayin day in the fourth month of Yongchu 2 a conflagration in Ayang, Hanyang, killed 3,570 people.

sentences.zh: 先是和帝崩，有皇子二人，皇子胜长，邓皇后贪殇帝少，欲自养长立之。

translations.literal: Before this, when Emperor He died there were two imperial sons; Prince Sheng was the elder; Empress Deng coveted Emperor Shang’s youth and wished to rear him herself and establish him when grown.
translations.idiomatic: After He’s death two princes survived; Liu Sheng was the elder, but Empress Deng preferred the infant Shang so she could prolong her regency.

sentences.zh: 延平元年，殇帝崩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanping, Emperor Shang died.
translations.idiomatic: The child emperor died in Yanping 1.

sentences.zh: 胜有厥疾不笃，群臣咸欲立之，太后以前既不立胜，遂更立清河王子，是为安帝。

translations.literal: Sheng had chronic ailments but was not gravely ill; the host of ministers all wished to enthrone him; because the empress dowager had earlier refused to establish Sheng, she thereupon instead set up the Prince of Qinghe’s son—this is Emperor An.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sheng was fit enough to rule, and the court wanted him, but the dowager—having once passed him over—enthroned the Qinghe prince’s son as Emperor An instead.

sentences.zh: 司空周章等心不厌服，谋欲诛邓氏，废太后、安帝，而更立胜。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Zhou Zhang and others inwardly did not submit; they plotted to execute the Deng clan, depose the empress dowager and Emperor An, and again enthrone Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhang and other ministers secretly planned a coup: wipe out the Deng family, depose regent and emperor, and restore Liu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 元年十一月，事觉，章等被诛。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year the affair was discovered; Zhang and the others were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The plot surfaced that eleventh month and the conspirators died.

sentences.zh: 其后凉州叛羌为害大甚，凉州诸郡寄治冯翊、扶风界。

translations.literal: Afterward the rebel Qiang of Liangzhou did harm on a great scale; the commanderies of Liangzhou were relocated for administration within the borders of Fengyi and Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Liangzhou Qiang revolted so fiercely that the northwestern commanderies had to be administered from Fengyi and Fufeng in the interior.

sentences.zh: 及太后崩，邓氏被诛。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager died, the Deng clan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: After the dowager’s death the Dengs were extirpated.

sentences.zh: 四年三月戊子，杜陵园火。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, third month, day wuzi, the park of the Du mausoleum burned.
translations.idiomatic: On a wuzi day in the third month of the fourth year fire swept Emperor Xuan’s Du necropolis.

sentences.zh: 元初四年二月壬戌，武库火。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanchu, second month, day renxu, the arsenal burned.
translations.idiomatic: The Han arsenal went up in flames on a renxu day in the second month of Yuanchu 4.

sentences.zh: 是时，羌叛，大为寇害，发天下兵以攻御之，积十余年未已，天下厌苦兵役。

translations.literal: At that time the Qiang rebelled and raided on a vast scale; the empire raised troops to attack and defend for more than ten years without end; all under Heaven wearied of military service.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang war had dragged on for over a decade; the realm groaned under endless levies.

sentences.zh: 延光元年八月戊子，阳陵园寝殿火。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanguang, eighth month, day wuzi, the shrine hall of the Yang mausoleum burned.
translations.idiomatic: On a wuzi day in the eighth month of Yanguang 1 fire consumed the resting hall at Emperor Jing’s Yang mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 凡灾发于先陵，此太子将废之象也。

translations.literal: Whenever disaster strikes the tombs of former emperors, it is an image of the heir apparent about to be deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Flames at an imperial tomb foretell a crown prince’s fall.

sentences.zh: 若曰：不当废太子以自剪，则火不当害先陵之寝也。

translations.literal: As if saying: if one ought not depose the heir apparent to cut one’s own posterity, then fire ought not harm the sleeping halls of the former mausolea.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven seemed to warn: strike the heir and you scorch your own ancestors’ sleep.

sentences.zh: 明年，上以谗言废皇太子为济阴王。

translations.literal: The next year, on slanderous words, the sovereign deposed the heir apparent as Prince of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor believed calumny and demoted the crown prince to prince of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 后二年，宫车宴驾。

translations.literal: After two more years the palace carriage feasted its late halt.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the emperor himself was dead.

sentences.zh: 中黄门孙程等十九人起兵殿省，诛贼臣，立济阴王。

translations.literal: Yellow-gate attendant Sun Cheng and eighteen others raised troops in the palace precincts, executed the wicked ministers, and enthroned the Prince of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cheng’s eunuch party struck, slew the usurping ministers, and restored the Jiyin prince to the throne.

sentences.zh: 四年秋七月乙丑，渔阳城门楼灾。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, autumn seventh month, day yichou, the Yuyang city gate tower burned.
translations.idiomatic: On a yichou day in the seventh month of the fourth year the Yuyang gate-tower burned.

sentences.zh: 顺帝永建三年七月丁酉，茂陵园寝灾。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shun’s third year of Yongjian, seventh month, day dingyou, the sleeping hall of the Mao mausoleum burned.
translations.idiomatic: On a dingyou day in the seventh month of Yongjian 3 fire damaged Emperor Wu’s Mao mausoleum hall.

sentences.zh: 阳嘉元年，恭陵庑灾，及东西莫府火。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yangjia, the Gongling portico burned, and east and west Mo offices caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: Yangjia 1 brought fire to Emperor An’s Gongling colonnades and to the east and west secretariat compounds.

sentences.zh: 太尉李固以为奢僭所致。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Li Gu held that it was caused by extravagance and usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu blamed luxury beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 陵之初造，祸及枯骨，规广治之尤饰。

translations.literal: When a mausoleum is first built, calamity reaches even dry bones—planning breadth and adornment are excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Tombs built too grandly call down disaster even on the dead—such was the excess of their scale and ornament.

sentences.zh: 又上欲更造宫室，益台观，故火起莫府。

translations.literal: Moreover the sovereign wished to rebuild palace chambers and increase terraces and belvederes; therefore fire arose in the Mo offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also meant to expand the palaces; hence the blaze in the ministerial offices.

sentences.zh: 烧材木。

translations.literal: It burned timber stores.
translations.idiomatic: The flames devoured the stockpiled lumber.

sentences.zh: 汉安元年三月甲午，雒阳刘汉等百九十七家为火所烧，后四年，宫车比三晏驾，建和元年君位乃定。

translations.literal: In the first year of Han’an, third month, day jiawu, one hundred ninety-seven households such as Liu Han of Luoyang were burned by fire; after four years the palace carriage in succession tarried thrice; only in the first year of Jianhe was the lord’s seat settled.
translations.idiomatic: On a jiawu day in the third month of Han’an 1 fire destroyed 197 Luoyang households including Liu Han’s; within four years three emperors died in quick succession, and the throne did not steady until Jianhe 1.

sentences.zh: 桓帝建和二年五月癸丑，北宫掖庭中德阳殿火，及左掖门。

translations.literal: In Huandi’s second year of Jianhe, fifth month, day guichou, the Deyang Hall in the northern palace’s lateral courts burned, reaching the left lateral gate.
translations.idiomatic: On a guichou day in the fifth month of Jianhe 2 fire swept the Deyang Hall in the harem and spread to the left yemen gate.

sentences.zh: 先是梁太后兄冀挟奸枉，以故太尉李固、杜乔正直，恐害其事，令人诬奏固、乔而诛灭之。

translations.literal: Before this, Empress Dowager Liang’s brother Ji carried favor to commit wicked perversions; because former grand commandants Li Gu and Du Qiao were upright and feared harm to his affairs, he had men falsely memorialize against Gu and Qiao and executed and exterminated them.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Ji had murdered Li Gu and Du Qiao on trumped-up charges to silence honest ministers.

sentences.zh: 是后梁太后崩，而梁氏诛灭。

translations.literal: Afterward Empress Dowager Liang died, and the Liang clan was executed and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Liang dowager’s death the whole clan was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 延熹四年正月辛酉，南宫嘉德殿火。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanxi, first month, day xinyou, the Jiade Hall of the Southern Palace burned.
translations.idiomatic: On a xinyou day in the first month of Yanxi 4 the Jiade Hall burned.

sentences.zh: 戊子，丙署火。

translations.literal: On day wuzi, the Bing office burned.
translations.idiomatic: The Bing office compound caught fire the same month on wuzi.

sentences.zh: 二月壬辰，武库火。

translations.literal: Second month, day renchen, the arsenal burned.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen in the second month the arsenal burned again.

sentences.zh: 五月丁卯，原陵长寿门火。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day dingmao, the Changshou Gate of the Yuan mausoleum burned.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao in the fifth month fire struck the Changshou Gate at Emperor Guangwu’s Yuan tomb.

sentences.zh: 先是，亳后因贱人得幸，号贵人。

translations.literal: Before this, the empress of Bo (亳), having through a lowly person obtained favor, was titled Honored Lady.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the future empress—here called the Lady of Bo—had won the emperor from the lowest ranks and borne the title Honored Lady.

sentences.zh: 为后。

translations.literal: She became empress.
translations.idiomatic: She was then raised to empress.

sentences.zh: 上以后母宣为长安君，封其兄弟，爱宠隆崇，又多封无功者。

translations.literal: The sovereign made the empress’s mother Xuan Lady Chang’an, enfeoffed her brothers, love and favor rose exceedingly high, and he also enfeoffed many without merit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ennobled Lady Xuan as Lady Chang’an, showered titles on her kin, and handed marquisates to favorites who had done nothing to earn them.

sentences.zh: 去年春，白马令李云坐直谏死。

translations.literal: Last spring, Prefect of Baima Li Yun sat guilty of blunt remonstrance and died.
translations.idiomatic: The year before, Li Yun of Baima had been executed for speaking plain truth to the throne.

sentences.zh: 至此彗除心、尾，火连作。

translations.literal: By here a comet had swept the Heart and Tail asterisms, and fires linked one after another.
translations.idiomatic: A comet had already scoured Heart and Tail; now fires chained across the capital.

sentences.zh: 五年正月壬午，南宫丙署火。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, first month, day renwu, the Bing office of the Southern Palace burned.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu in the first month of Yanxi 5 the Southern Palace’s Bing office burned.

sentences.zh: 四月乙丑，恭北陵东阙火。

translations.literal: Fourth month, day yichou, the east que of Gongbei mausoleum burned.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou in the fourth month fire damaged the east tower of Emperor An’s tomb.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，虎贲掖门火。

translations.literal: On day wuchen, the Tiger-Gaurd lateral gate burned.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the Tiger-Gaurd side gate caught fire.

sentences.zh: 五月，康陵园寝火。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Kang mausoleum shrine burned.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangling hall burned in the fifth month.

sentences.zh: 甲申，中藏府承禄署火。

translations.literal: On day jiashen, the Cheng-lu office of the inner treasury burned.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the Cheng-lu office in the imperial treasury went up in flames.

sentences.zh: 七月己未，南宫承善闼内火。

translations.literal: Seventh month, day jiwei, fire inside the Chengshan gate-tower of the Southern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei in the seventh month fire broke out inside the Chengshan gate of the Southern Palace.

sentences.zh: 六年四月辛亥，康陵东署火。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, fourth month, day xinhai, the east office of Kang mausoleum burned.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai in the fourth month of the sixth year Kangling’s east annex burned.

sentences.zh: 七月甲申，平陵园寝火。

translations.literal: Seventh month, day jiashen, the Ping mausoleum shrine burned.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen in the seventh month the Pingling resting hall caught fire.

sentences.zh: 八年二月己酉，南宫嘉德署、黄龙、千秋万岁殿皆火。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, second month, day jiyou, the Jiade office, Yellow Dragon Hall, and Hall of Myriad Years of the Southern Palace all burned.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou in the second month of the eighth year three major Southern Palace structures burned together.

sentences.zh: 四月甲寅，安陵园寝火。

translations.literal: Fourth month, day jiayin, the An mausoleum shrine burned.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin in the fourth month Anling’s hall burned.

sentences.zh: 闰月，南宫长秋、和欢殿后钩盾、掖庭朔平署各火。

translations.literal: Intercalary month: the Changqiu, Hehuan halls, rear Gou-shield, and Shuoping office of the lateral courts each burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the leap month fires separately struck the Changqiu and Hehuan halls and rear harem offices.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬子，德阳前殿西阁及黄门北寺火，殺人。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day renzi, the west pavilion of the Deyang front hall and the Northern Office of the Yellow Gates burned, killing people.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi in the eleventh month flames took the Deyang Hall’s west wing and the eunuchs’ North Prison, with loss of life.

sentences.zh: 九年三月癸己，京都夜有火光转行，民相惊噪。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, third month, day guisi, at night in the capital there were streaks of fire-light moving; the people alarmed one another with shouts.
translations.idiomatic: On a guisi night in the third month of the ninth year Luoyang saw wandering will-o’-wisp lights and panicked crowds.

sentences.zh: 灵帝熹平四年五月，延陵园灾。

translations.literal: In Lingdi’s fourth year of Xiping, fifth month, the Yan mausoleum suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Xiping 4 Emperor Shun’s Yan mausoleum burned.

sentences.zh: 光和四年闰月辛酉，北宫东掖庭永巷署灾。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guanghe, intercalary month, day xinyou, the Yongxiang office in the eastern lateral courts of the Northern Palace burned.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou in the leap month of Guanghe 4 fire destroyed the Yongxiang harem office in the Northern Palace.

sentences.zh: 五年五月庚申，德阳前殿西北入门内永乐太后宫署火。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day gengshen, the Yongle empress dowager’s offices inside the northwest entry of the Deyang front hall burned.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the fifth month Lady Dong’s Yongle apartments beside Deyang Hall caught fire.

sentences.zh: 中平二年二月己酉，南宫云台灾。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongping, second month, day jiyou, the Cloud Terrace of the Southern Palace burned.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou in the second month of Zhongping 2 the Southern Palace’s Cloud Terrace burned.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，乐成门灾，延及北阙，度道西烧嘉德、和欢殿。

translations.literal: On day gengxu, the Lecheng Gate burned, extending to the north que, crossing the west road and burning Jiade and Hehuan halls.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Lecheng Gate fire spread through the north tower and west avenue to Jiade and Hehuan.

sentences.zh: 案云台之灾自上起，榱题数百，同时并然，若就县华镫，其日烧尽，延及白虎、威兴门、尚书、符節、兰台。

translations.literal: Examining the Cloud Terrace disaster: it began from above; several hundred bracket-heads at once caught fire as if dipped in hanging flowered lamps; that day it burned out, extending to White Tiger and Weixing gates, the secretariat, tally office, and Orchid Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: The Cloud Terrace blaze started at the roofline; hundreds of corbels ignited like candles on a chandelier and in one day consumed the terrace, then raced to the White Tiger and Weixing gates and the central archives.

sentences.zh: 夫云台者，乃周家之所造也，图书、术籍、珍玩、宝怪皆所藏在也。

translations.literal: The Cloud Terrace was built by the house of Zhou; books, charts, occult writings, curios, and treasures were stored there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou had raised that terrace to house the imperial libraries and rare treasures.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「君不思道，厥妖火烧宫。

translations.literal: Jing Fang’s Commentary on the Changes says: "When the lord does not ponder the Way, its prodigy is fire burning the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang warns that a ruler who abandons the Way will watch his palace burn.

sentences.zh: 」是时，黄巾作慝，变乱天常，七州二十八郡同时俱发，命将出众，虽颇有所禽，然宛、广宗、曲阳尚未破坏，役起负海，杼柚空悬，百姓死伤已过半矣。

translations.literal: " At that time the Yellow Turbans wrought evil, overturning Heaven’s constant; seven provinces and twenty-eight commanderies rose together; ordered generals went out with hosts; although they took some captives, yet Wan, Guangzong, and Quyang were not yet broken; service rose from the sea’s edge; shuttles hung empty; the common people’s dead and wounded already exceeded half.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Turban revolt convulsed twenty-eight commanderies; imperial generals won only partial success while great strongholds held out; levies emptied every workshop and killed or maimed more than half the populace.

sentences.zh: 而灵帝曾不克己复礼，虐侈滋甚，尺一雨布，驺骑电激，官非其人，政以贿成，内嬖鸿都，并受封爵。

translations.literal: Yet Lingdi was never able to restrain himself and return to ritual; cruel extravagance grew worse; foot-long edicts and rain of cloth; mounted messengers like lightning; offices not given to the right men; government completed by bribes; inner favorites of Hongdu together received noble ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling only deepened his excess—lavish edicts, courier relays racing night and day, offices sold to the highest bidder, and Hongdu favorites ennobled wholesale.

sentences.zh: 京都为之语曰：「今兹诸侯岁也。

translations.literal: The capital made a saying of it: "This year is the year of the many marquises."
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang jeered, "This season—everyone’s a marquis."

sentences.zh: 」天戒若曰：放贤赏淫，何以旧典为？

translations.literal: Heaven’s warning was as if saying: casting away worthies and rewarding debauchery—what use are the old canons?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven seemed to ask why any statute mattered when virtue was banished and vice ennobled.

sentences.zh: 故焚其台门秘府也。

translations.literal: Therefore it burned the terrace gates and secret treasury.
translations.idiomatic: So it consumed the terrace gates and the archives they guarded.

sentences.zh: 其后三年，灵帝暴崩，续以董卓之乱，火三日不绝，京都为丘墟矣。

translations.literal: After three more years Lingdi suddenly died; continuing with Dong Zhuo’s turmoil, fire three days did not cease; the capital became mounds and ruins.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years the emperor was dead; Dong Zhuo’s occupation left Luoyang burning three days until nothing remained but rubble.

sentences.zh: 献帝初平元年八月，霸桥灾。

translations.literal: In Xiandi’s first year of Chuping, eighth month, the Ba Bridge burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Chuping 1 the Ba Bridge burned.

sentences.zh: 其后三年，董卓见殺。

translations.literal: After three years Dong Zhuo was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later Dong Zhuo lay dead.

sentences.zh: 庶征之恒燠，《汉书》以冬温应之。

translations.literal: Among the many portents, constant heat—the Book of Han paired winter warmth with it.
translations.idiomatic: The Han treatise matched unseasonable winter warmth to the "constant heat" omen.

sentences.zh: 中兴以来，亦有冬温，而记不录云。

translations.literal: Since the restoration there has also been winter warmth, but the annals do not record it.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Han knew warm winters too, though the compilers left them unlogged.

sentences.zh: 安帝元初三年，有瓜异本共生，八瓜同蒂，时以为嘉瓜。

translations.literal: In Emperor An’s third year of Yuanchu, melons of different stems grew together from one root, eight melons on one peduncle; the time took them for auspicious melons.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchu 3 produced a freak vine: eight gourds on one stem, hailed at first as a good omen.

sentences.zh: 或以为瓜者外延，离本而实，女子外属之象也。

translations.literal: Some held that melons are outward extension, leaving the root yet bearing fruit—an image of women’s external kin.
translations.idiomatic: Skeptics read the gourd as a symbol of affinal power branching from the court.

sentences.zh: 是时，阎皇后初立，后阎后与外亲耿宝等共谮太子，废为济阴王，更外迎济北王子犊立之，草妖也。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Yan had just been established; afterward Empress Yan with outer kin Geng Bao and others together slandered the heir apparent, deposed him as Prince of Jiyin, and outwardly brought in the Prince of Jibei’s son Du to establish him—a grass prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yan had just risen; she and Geng Bao framed the crown prince, demoted him, and imported the Jibei boy Liu Du—exactly the "grass prodigy" reading.

sentences.zh: 桓帝延熹九年，雒阳城局竹柏叶有伤者。

translations.literal: In Huandi’s ninth year of Yanxi, bamboo and cypress leaves within the Luoyang wall wards showed wounds.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanxi 9 leaves of bamboo and cypress inside Luoyang’s wards bore strange scars.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「天子凶。」

translations.literal: Divination said: "The Son of Heaven is in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Soothsayers pronounced doom on the throne.

sentences.zh: 灵帝熹平三年，右校别作中有两樗树，皆高四尺所，其一株宿夕暴长，长丈余，大一围，作胡人状，头目鬓须发备具。

translations.literal: In Lingdi’s third year of Xiping, inside the Right Camp’s separate works two ailanthus trees, both about four chi high—one overnight suddenly grew to more than a zhang, one arm’s girth, shaped like a Hu man, with head, eyes, beard, and hair complete.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiping 3 a pair of ailanthus saplings in the right camp workshops shot overnight into a man-shaped tree the height of a Hu barbarian, complete in face and hair.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「王德衰，下人将起，则有木生人状。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang’s Commentary on the Changes says: "When kingly virtue declines and the lower people are about to rise, then there is wood that grows in human shape."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang marks such growths as omens of popular uprising when royal virtue fails.

sentences.zh: 五年十月壬午，御所居殿后槐树，皆六七围，自拔，倒竖，根在上。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, tenth month, day renwu, locust trees behind the hall where the sovereign dwelled, all six or seven arm-girths, uprooted themselves, inverted, roots upward.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu in the tenth month of Xiping 5 the great locust trees behind the imperial bedchamber tore loose and stood on their crowns, roots in the air.

sentences.zh: 中平元年夏，东郡，陈留济阳、长桓，济阴冤句、离狐县界，有草生，其茎靡累肿大，如手指，状似鸠雀龙蛇鸟兽之形，五色各如其状，毛羽头目足翅皆具。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongping, summer, along the borders of Dong commandery, Chenliu’s Jiyang and Changhuan, and Jiyin’s Yuanqu and Ligou, grass grew whose stalks twined and swelled like fingers, shaped like doves, sparrows, dragons, snakes, birds, and beasts; each of five colors matched its shape; fur, feathers, head, eyes, feet, and wings were all present.
translations.idiomatic: That summer freak grass sprang up along the Ji River borderlands, sprouting finger-thick stalks molded like birds and beasts in five colors, every feather and claw distinct.

sentences.zh: 近草妖也。

translations.literal: This was near a grass prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: The annalist classes it with grass prodigies.

sentences.zh: 是岁，黄巾贼始起。

translations.literal: That year the Yellow Turban bandits first rose.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Yellow Turbans rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 皇后兄何进，异父兄朱苗，皆为将军，领兵。

translations.literal: The empress’s elder brother He Jin and her elder uterine brother Zhu Miao were both generals commanding troops.
translations.idiomatic: Empress He’s brother He Jin and her half-brother Zhu Miao each held generalships and led armies.

sentences.zh: 后苗封济阴侯，进、苗遂秉威权，特国柄，汉遂微弱，自此始焉。

translations.literal: Later Miao was enfeoffed marquis of Jiyin; Jin and Miao thereupon grasped awesomeness and power, monopolized the state handle, and Han thereupon grew weak—beginning from this.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Miao became marquis of Jiyin, he and He Jin seized the levers of power and the dynasty began its slide.

sentences.zh: 中平中，长安城西北六七里空树中，有人面生鬓。

translations.literal: In the Zhongping era, in a hollow tree six or seven li northwest of Chang’an city, a human face with sideburns grew.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhongping a hollow tree northwest of Chang’an sprouted a bearded human face in its cavity.

sentences.zh: 献帝兴平元年九月，桑复生椹，可食。

translations.literal: In Xiandi’s first year of Xingping, ninth month, mulberries again bore fruit fit to eat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Xingping 1 mulberries fruited out of season—sweet enough to eat.

sentences.zh: 安帝延光三年二月戊子，有五色大鸟集济南台，十月，又集新丰，时以为凤皇。

translations.literal: In Emperor An’s third year of Yanguang, second month, day wuzi, a great five-colored bird alighted on the terrace in Jinan; in the tenth month it again alighted at Xinfeng; the time took it for a phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi in the second month of Yanguang 3 a huge polychrome bird perched on Jinan’s terrace and again at Xinfeng—courtiers hailed it as a phoenix.

sentences.zh: 或以为凤皇阳明之应，故非明主，则隐不见。

translations.literal: Some held that the phoenix is the response of yang brightness; therefore if it is not a bright lord, it hides and does not appear.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued a true phoenix appears only under a sage-king; otherwise it stays hidden.

sentences.zh: 凡五色大鸟似凤者，多羽虫之孽。

translations.literal: In general great five-colored birds resembling phoenixes are for the most part winged-insect prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: Such rainbow birds are usually classed as winged omens, not true phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 是时，安帝信中常侍樊丰、江京、阿母王圣及外属耿宝等谗言，免太尉杨震，废太子为济阴王，不悊之异也。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor An trusted palace attendants Fan Feng, Jiang Jing, nurse Wang Sheng, and outer kin Geng Bao and others’ slanderous words, dismissed Grand Commandant Yang Zhen, and deposed the heir apparent as Prince of Jiyin—a prodigy of lack of discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An was listening to Fan Feng, Jiang Jing, Wang Sheng, and Geng Bao: he cashiered Yang Zhen and cast down the crown prince—exactly the blindness those birds foretold.

sentences.zh: 章帝末，号凤皇百四十九见。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhangdi’s reign, phoenixes were titled one hundred forty-nine sightings.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Zhang’s reign the court logged 149 “phoenix” sightings.

sentences.zh: 时，直臣何敞以为羽孽，似凤，翱翔殿屋，不察也。

translations.literal: At the time straight minister He Chang held them to be winged prodigies, resembling phoenixes, soaring over palace roofs—lack of inspection.
translations.idiomatic: He Chang called them counterfeit phoenixes wheeling over the halls—omens no one cared to read.

sentences.zh: 记者以为其后章帝崩，以为验。

translations.literal: The recorder thought that afterward Zhangdi died and took it as verification.
translations.idiomatic: The compiler notes that Emperor Zhang soon died—proof, he thought, of ill omen.

sentences.zh: 案宣帝、明帝时，五色鸟群翔殿屋，贾逵以为胡降征也。

translations.literal: Examining: in the times of Emperors Xuan and Ming, flocks of five-colored birds soared over palace halls; Jia Kui held it to be the sign of surrender of the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuandi and Mingdi similar flocks had appeared; Jia Kui read them as portents of barbarian submission.

sentences.zh: 帝多善政，虽有过，不及至衰缺，末年胡降二十万口，是其验也。

translations.literal: Those emperors had many good policies; although they had faults, they did not reach decline and want; in the last years the Hu surrendered two hundred thousand persons—this was its verification.
translations.idiomatic: Those were strong reigns; when 200,000 tribesmen submitted late in the era, Jia Kui’s reading seemed vindicated.

sentences.zh: 帝之时，羌胡外叛，谗慝内兴，羽孽之时也。

translations.literal: In this emperor’s time, Qiang and Hu rebelled outside while slander flourished within—the season of winged prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: Under An the frontiers rose in revolt and calumny filled the palace—the age of false phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 《乐叶图征》说五凤皆五色，为瑞者一，为孽者四。

translations.literal: The Music Leaf Chart Prognostication says the five phoenixes are all five-colored: one is auspicious, four are prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: The weft-text on the five phoenixes counts one bird as lucky and four as baleful.

sentences.zh: 桓帝元嘉元年十一月，五色大鸟见济阴己氏。

translations.literal: In Huandi’s first year of Yuanjia, eleventh month, a great five-colored bird appeared at Yishi in Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Yuanjia 1 a polychrome giant bird showed itself at Yishi in Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 时以为凤皇。

translations.literal: The time took it for a phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: Again the court cried phoenix.

sentences.zh: 此时政治衰缺，梁冀秉政阿枉，上幸毫后，皆羽孽时也。

translations.literal: At this time government was in decline and want; Liang Ji held power and bent justice; the sovereign favored the empress of Bo—all a season of winged prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: Government was rotten, Liang Ji twisted the law, and the emperor doted on Empress Deng—another season of winged ill omens.

sentences.zh: 灵帝光和四年秋，五色大鸟见于新城，众鸟随之，时以为凤皇。

translations.literal: In Lingdi’s fourth year of Guanghe, autumn, a great five-colored bird appeared in Xincheng, a host of birds following it; the time took it for a phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Guanghe 4 a giant polychrome bird appeared at Xincheng with a flock in train—again mistaken for a phoenix.

sentences.zh: 时，灵帝不恤政事，常侍、黄门专权，羽孽之时也。

translations.literal: At that time Lingdi did not pity government affairs; regular attendants and yellow-gate eunuchs monopolized power—the season of winged prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ling ignored the state while eunuchs ran it—another “winged prodigy” age.

sentences.zh: 众鸟之性，见非常班驳，好聚观之，至于小爵希见枭者，虣见犹聚。

translations.literal: The nature of the many birds is: when they see something unusually mottled, they love to gather and watch it; as for small sparrows that seldom see owls, when they suddenly see one they still gather.
translations.idiomatic: Birds flock to anything gaudy; even sparrows will mob an owl on rare sight—so the mob followed the monster bird.

sentences.zh: 中平三年八月中，怀陵上有万余爵，先极悲鸣，已因乱斗相殺，皆断头，悬著树枝枳棘。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Zhongping, on the Hui mausoleum mound more than ten thousand sparrows first cried most mournfully, then thereupon tangled in disorder fighting and killing one another, all decapitated, hanging from branches of thorn.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongping 3’s eighth month ten thousand sparrows on Emperor Huai’s tumulus wailed, then tore one another apart until headless corpses hung from the brambles.

sentences.zh: 到六年，灵帝崩，大将军何进以内宠外嬖，积恶日久，欲悉纠黜，以隆更始冗政，而太后持疑，事久不决。

translations.literal: When it reached the sixth year, Lingdi died; great general He Jin, because inner favorites and outer minions had piled up evil a long time, wished to investigate and dismiss them all to elevate a renewed beginning and cut redundant government, but the empress dowager held doubt and the affair long was not decided.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhongping 6 the emperor was dead; He Jin meant to purge palace favorites of long standing, but the dowager hesitated and the coup stalled.

sentences.zh: 进从中出，于省内见殺，因是有司荡涤虔刘，后禄而尊厚者无余矣。

translations.literal: Jin came out from within and was killed in the palace precincts; thereupon responsible offices swept and slaughtered; afterward those with stipends and honored thickness had none left.
translations.idiomatic: He Jin walked into the inner palace and died; then came the great slaughter until no great house survived unscathed.

sentences.zh: 夫陵者，高大之象也。

translations.literal: A mound is an image of height and greatness.
translations.idiomatic: A royal tumulus stands for eminence and power.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰：诸怀爵禄而尊厚者，还自相害至灭亡也。

translations.literal: Heaven’s warning was as if saying: those who harbor noble rank and honored thickness will in the end harm one another to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven warned that title-fat nobles would destroy one another to the last man.

sentences.zh: 桓帝建和三年秋七月，北地廉雨肉似羊肋，或大如手。

translations.literal: In Huandi’s third year of Jianhe, autumn seventh month, in Beidi there fell in continuous rain flesh like sheep ribs, some as large as a hand.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Jianhe 3 a red rain of meat—lumps like mutton ribs, some palm-sized—fell on Beidi.

sentences.zh: 近赤祥也。

translations.literal: This was near a red auspice.
translations.idiomatic: The annalist classes it with crimson spectral omens.

sentences.zh: 是时梁太后摄政，兄梁冀专权，枉诛汉良臣故太尉李固、杜乔，天下冤之。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Liang held the regency; her brother Liang Ji monopolized power and on false charges executed Han’s good ministers, former grand commandants Li Gu and Du Qiao; all under Heaven thought it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Liang ruled through Liang Ji, who murdered Li Gu and Du Qiao—the realm cried injustice.

sentences.zh: 其后梁氏诛灭。

translations.literal: Afterward the Liang clan was executed and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Liangs were soon extirpated.
